newsitem.title: UK: Germany says cocoa import statistics may be flawed.
newsitem.headline: Germany says cocoa import statistics may be flawed.

text.p: German industry officials said on Friday statistical data on imports of cocoa beans could be flawed due to the complex trade logistics within the European single market.

A group of experts meeting on Thursday under the umbrella of the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) brought into focus a long-standing trade speculation that German cocoa stocks could be under-reported due to inaccurate grind figures.

By 1995/96 a discrepancy of some 130,000 tonnes emerged between the stock estimates of the ICCO and the UK trade house E.D.&F. Man which uses bean imports to monitor stocks instead of grindings. But Karsten Keunecke, managing director of the German confectionery industry association BDS, said the problem could be rooted in possible errors in bean import statistics384 "I think the mistake is rather in imports than grindings," Keunecke told Reuters on the last day of ICCO talks.

"We have tried to look at whether the people who give us the grindings are giving us the right figures. We get data from all German processors and I have no reason to believe that they are not supplying the right figures," he said.
Cocoa imports into Germany gathered by the European statistics body Intrastat have significantly exceeded domestic grindings in the last five years.

Keunecke said one reason could be double counting in imports as the big chunk of cocoa in Germany is not directly shipped from source but re-routed via the Netherlands -- Europe's hub of cocoa processing -- Belgium and France.
Intrastat had agreed to review its process of consolodating data to see whether improvements can be made.
The ICCO estimated stocks in German ports and warehouses at 87,000 tonnes in September 1996.
Hagen Streichert of the German Ministry of Agriculture who leads the German delegation also undertook an overhaul of domestic reporting sources to try to correct any possible errors in grinds.
Analysts said the German cocoa usage could be somewhere between grindings and imports. But some doubted the relevance of revisions in stocks estimates.
"There are no stocks in Germany anyway," said Streichert.
The ICCO uses two weeks of annual grindings to calculate manufacturers' working stocks in Western Europe.
German cocoa bean imports in the January-July period of 1996 totalled 157,737 tonnes.
